kept.title: The two causal memory wins: cold 0/10 & 0/8, warm 8.8/10 & 8/8 (blind-graded)
kept.summary: On held-out edge cases the agent never saw, the cold/OFF arm scored 0/10 and 0/8 with ZERO variance; the warm/ON arm scored 8.8/10 and 8/8 and wrote 3.8x and 1.7x MORE code citing the seeded note — so the effect is retrieve-and-apply (added capability), not shortcutting. This is the load-bearing result the whole memory-RAG program rests on.

kept.title: Memory is load-bearing iff knowledge is empirical AND external-to-artifact AND project-local
kept.summary: All three conditions are necessary. Counterexamples that each break one: v4 (general verdict didn't help — not empirical), wincase-c/silent-cap (in-worktree test or dependency source IS the oracle — not external), Phase 1 (mkcert issuer-trust, don't-clobber-native-files, GC retention, stale-claim hygiene — general knowledge already in the model's prior, so cold passed every edge, proxy precision 0/4).

kept.title: Rigging guard 'cold must fail before warm runs' is the honesty mechanism — it killed 3 trap classes
kept.summary: Every held-out experiment requires the cold arm to genuinely fail before a warm win can be claimed. This guard caught wincase-c, silent-cap, and all four Phase 1 traps as false wins (cold solved them by reading the committed oracle). Eight nulls plus guard discipline is WHY the two real wins are believable — the failure modes are the trust mechanism, not embarrassments to bury.

kept.title: The oracle leak: every bench v1–v8 shipped its own answer key into the worktree
kept.summary: An in-worktree acceptance test or dependency source IS the oracle — the agent reverse-engineers the strategy from asserted behavior no matter how strategy-silent the prose spec is. So all of v1–v8 systematically OVERSTATED self-solvability (cold arms graded themselves against a visible answer). Fix: the held-out protocol (scripts/bench-heldout.js) gives prose spec only and grades with an external suite the agent never sees. Production is naturally held-out.

kept.title: Context gate abstains on all 11 negatives at regret 0, avoiding ~690,510 tok-eq of inject tax
kept.summary: The context-need gate (default ABSTAIN) refuses injection on all 11 negative-labeled tasks with zero regret, avoiding ~690,510 token-equivalents of the over-deliberation tax the always-inject arms paid (forced full-payload injection cost 1.63x and up to a ~2x hardness tax monotone in amount injected).

kept.title: Context-gate shipped DEFAULTS: cos 0.50, gap 0.25, margin 0.08, empirical=true, locality 2
kept.summary: lib/context-gate.js DEFAULTS: cosThreshold 0.50 (lowered from 0.55 because the first real positive sat at 0.548), gapThreshold 0.25, marginThreshold 0.08 (alt path), requireEmpirical true, localityThreshold 2. INJECT iff top1>=0.50 AND top note empirical AND (gap>=0.25 OR margin>=0.08) AND projectLocality>=2; else ABSTAIN. These are provisional, calibrated on n=1 positive.

kept.title: external-gap (not cosine/margin) is the gate's discriminator — MiniLM packs notes into a 0.50–0.55 band
kept.summary: MiniLM pulls topically-adjacent orchestrator notes into a tight 0.50–0.55 cosine band where neither cosine nor margin can separate a load-bearing note from topical noise. The discriminating signal is external-gap: the fraction of the note's own content tokens that recur in the task text — 0.34 for the on-task scar vs <=0.17 for every plain topical negative.

kept.title: projectLocality scores 4 regex categories (measured/errval/ident/observed); gate requires >=2
kept.summary: Phase 1's third boundary (project-locality) is operationalized as a 0–4 count over measured (percentages/ratios), errval (NaN/error codes/quoted data with digits), ident (camelCase/snake_case/file paths/function calls), and observed-on-real-data language. Winners score 3–4; pretraining-prior false-injects score 0–1; only ~14% of the live KB scores >=2. The locality regex structurally can't see migration-schema facts phrased without identifiers/observational language (legacy-id false-negative).

kept.title: Judge cost is infrastructure capex, tracked separately — never in per-task ON_cost
kept.summary: The judge drain runs in a SEPARATE harness session, so its tokens never appear in ON_cost. The system ledger (bench/economy/ledger.json) tracks cumulative savings vs judge infrastructure spend as a separate line — judge tokens are not amortized per task.

kept.title: Judge edge value fans out transitively through the DAG, so per-edge amortization is impossible
kept.summary: A note that improves Task A's summary also benefits every downstream task inheriting A as context, so judge-edge value cannot be amortized per edge. The correct accounting unit is the system ledger's total-savings-vs-total-spend, not any per-task or per-edge ratio.

kept.title: needs_context label = cold(OFF) NEVER solved AND warm(ON) solved (held-out derivation)
kept.summary: Phase 1 / held-out ground truth defines needs_context as the strong criterion: cold arm never solved across all trials AND warm arm solved. Derived from bench/heldout/p1/results.jsonl. This is the stricter of the two label schemes used in this repo.

kept.title: GOTCHA: two different needs_context label derivations across the benchmark reports
kept.summary: The v1–v7 benchmark headline labels needs_context by a cost-weighted metric (ON underperforms OFF), while Phase 1 held-out uses the stronger 'cold arm never solved' criterion. They reach consistent gate verdicts but are NOT the same definition — don't conflate the two when reading numbers across reports.

kept.title: Same-micro-domain controls fire the gate but are excluded from regret on temporal grounds
kept.summary: graph-dependent and wincase-c retrieve the SAME note as the positive and are textually NEARER to it, so the recalibrated gate fires on them (2/2). They are NOT counted in scoped regret only because the note post-dates them (it could not have been retrieved at their run time). This proves a structural limit: a note<->task gate cannot detect held-out-ness — that property is environmental, external to the gate's inputs.

kept.title: resolveOwner win rests on ~40% of registry records lacking a session, recoverable only via byWindow
kept.summary: The task-transcript / resolveOwner held-out win: the spec describes only direct + session resolution, but ~40% of this registry's agent records have no session and are recoverable ONLY by time-window-overlap correlation against byWindow. That fact lives in a pre-seeded note (originally note-mq7kyiir6sx); the OFF arm must derive the strategy from scratch and never references byWindow.

kept.title: Standing caveat: the corpus is maximally self-similar (orchestrator benchmarking itself)
kept.summary: All benchmark numbers come from one operator running the orchestrator instrumenting its OWN memory system — maximally self-similar. What transfers to a customer project is the CATEGORY (every project accumulates its own local empirical facts), not the notes themselves and not necessarily the 23% point estimate.

kept.title: Winnable regime is ~23% (12/52) of note-dependent tasks — the project-local-measured slice
kept.summary: Phase 0a found 18/52 'winnable' (external-gap + empirical + load-bearing), splitting them 12 'benchmark-meta' (project-local measured verdicts) vs 6 'transfer-robust general-infra'. Phase 1 INVERTED Phase 0a's bet: the general-infra slice is exactly what pretraining covers (0/4 traps survived), while the project-local-meta slice is where both real wins live. Honest frequency = ~23% (12/52), not the general-infra slice Phase 0a guessed at ~10–15%.

kept.title: v7: the combined DAG+RAG arm was the WORST; hardness grows monotone in context amount
kept.summary: First real semantic RAG (MiniLM) + DAG context, 4 arms x 2 tasks: NO win on all 6 ON cells, and the combined DAG+RAG arm was the worst. Hardness rose monotonically with amount injected (v4: H_off 14,584 -> search 16,274 -> lean 19,969 -> dagrag 29,027, ~2x). Solve rate stayed 100% everywhere — context only added deliberation. v7 also closed the retrieval-quality alibi: semantic retrieval demonstrably worked and changed nothing; the blocker was never recall.

kept.title: Vendor '90% token savings' is strawman-relative; prompt caching already gives both arms memory-like cost
kept.summary: The audited ~90% memory-product savings compare against replaying full conversation history every turn — a baseline nobody competent runs. Under claude -p, prompt-cache reads bill at ~0.1x input and climb monotonically within a session, so the harness gives memory-like cost behavior to BOTH arms for free. Against real baselines the savings evaporate; cost difference was purely cache_read on the injected payload, with output tokens (real work) unmoved.
